answer: Because the ledge index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the crystal audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the raven identifier and voids the later submissions, and therefore the operator pays for 144 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 144 answers need 144 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
